name: Kerala
tagline: Tea hills, tiger country, and a night asleep on the backwaters
hero_description: Kerala strings together landscapes that shouldn't fit in one state: mist-cool tea plantations at Munnar, boat-safari wildlife on Periyar Lake, and the canal-veined backwaters of Alleppey — where you sleep aboard a converted rice barge as village life drifts past. Add 500 years of trading history at Fort Kochi and Ayurveda done properly, and it earns the hype.
best_time_to_visit: October to March — 18–30°C with post-monsoon greenery and reliable weather for backwater cruising; monsoon (June–September) is the traditional season for Ayurvedic treatment, when therapies are considered most effective.

top_attractions.name: Alleppey Backwaters
top_attractions.description: A maze of canals, lagoons and paddy-field villages around Vembanad Lake, cruised overnight aboard kettuvallams — traditional rice barges converted into houseboats with bedrooms, a deck and an onboard cook.

top_attractions.name: Munnar
top_attractions.description: A tea town sitting at roughly 1,450–1,600 m in the Western Ghats, wrapped in plantation contours; neighbouring Eravikulam National Park protects the endangered Nilgiri tahr, under Anamudi — at 2,695 m the highest peak in peninsular India.

top_attractions.name: Periyar Tiger Reserve, Thekkady
top_attractions.description: One of India's few reserves where the safari happens by boat — cruises on Periyar Lake pass elephants and gaur at the waterline, with cardamom and pepper plantations at the park's edge.

top_attractions.name: Fort Kochi
top_attractions.description: A 16th-century European trading enclave where shore-operated Chinese fishing nets line the harbour and St. Francis Church (1503) — India's oldest European church — once held Vasco da Gama's remains.

top_attractions.name: Kathakali performance
top_attractions.description: Kerala's classical dance-drama, staged nightly at Kochi's cultural centres — arrive an hour early to watch performers apply the elaborate green make-up that defines the art form.

top_attractions.name: Athirappilly Falls
top_attractions.description: A broad curtain of water about 24 m high on the Chalakudy River — widely called Kerala's largest waterfall and at full roar in and just after the monsoon.

activities: Overnight houseboat cruise on the Alleppey backwaters with onboard Kerala meals
Tea-estate walk and tea museum visit in Munnar
Boat safari on Periyar Lake at Thekkady
Spice garden tour in cardamom country
Ayurvedic massage or multi-day wellness programme
Sunset at the Chinese fishing nets in Fort Kochi
Village shikara canoe ride through Alleppey's narrow canals
A sadya feast served on a banana leaf
